images.caption:
Acha Mor This image illustrates well the origins of the place name Acha Mor. The photograph is taken in the middle of the "Acha" which literally means "field" and when coupled with the word "Mor" translates as "Big Field".
The TV mast on Eitseal Hill 223m and plantations near the village are also shown.
images.alt:
Acha Mor This image illustrates well the origins of the place name Acha Mor. The photograph is taken in the middle of the "Acha" which literally means "field" and when coupled with the word "Mor" translates as "Big Field".
The TV mast on Eitseal Hill 223m and plantations near the village are also shown.

images.caption: Abhainn Cheann Chuisil stream The rocky curve is the stream running down from the mountains on the island of Harris in the Outer Hebrides. The surrounding vegetation is soft peat and bog amongst the rocks. In the distance the hills can be seen to be misty due to rainfall.
images.alt: Abhainn Cheann Chuisil stream The rocky curve is the stream running down from the mountains on the island of Harris in the Outer Hebrides. The surrounding vegetation is soft peat and bog amongst the rocks. In the distance the hills can be seen to be misty due to rainfall.
